title: Assistant Management Accountant (PQ)
description:
Assistant Management Accountant

Location: Waterloo, London (SE1)

Salary: Competitive + Bonus + Excellent Benefits

Join a High-Growth Global Technology Business

We're seeking a driven and detail-oriented Assistant Management Accountant to join a fast-growing international technology organisation. This is an exciting opportunity for someone looking to develop their career within a dynamic, innovative, and collaborative finance environment.

Working closely with the Finance Manager and Group Reporting team, you'll play a key role in supporting month-end reporting, financial analysis, compliance activities, and process improvements across multiple international entities.

About You

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical accounting knowledge with a proactive and analytical mindset.

You will have:
- Good understanding of accruals, prepayments, journals, balance sheet reconciliations and month-end processes.
- Part-qualified (no more than 6 exams passed) ACCA, CIMA, or equivalent.
- Previous experience (one to three years) in an Assistant Accountant, Assistant Management Accountant, or similar role.
- Strong Excel skills (Pivots, LookUps)
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.
- A desire to learn, improve processes, and develop professionally.
- Experience within a multi-entity or international business would be advantageous.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Analysis & Reporting
- Perform monthly P&L analysis and investigate key variances.
- Prepare month-end reporting commentary and financial insights.
- Maintain and reconcile balance sheet accounts.
- Support ad-hoc analysis, reporting, and finance projects.

Month-End Close & Cost Management
- Prepare accruals and prepayments.
- Assist with fixed asset accounting.
- Support purchase ledger activities and cost coding.
- Review outstanding costs and support accurate month-end reporting.
- Contribute to group-wide month-end activities across multiple entities.

Audit & Compliance
- Support external audit processes and information requests.
- Assist with VAT calculations and statutory submissions.
- Contribute to corporate tax reporting requirements.
- Maintain strong financial controls and documentation standards.

Process Improvement
- Identify opportunities to improve finance processes and reporting efficiency.
- Support the implementation and adoption of finance systems and automation tools.

What's on Offer?
- Annual bonus scheme
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays and birthday leave
- Private medical cover including dental and optical benefits
- Pension contribution
- Life assurance and income protection
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Work-from-anywhere opportunities

Apply Now

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an ambitious, rapidly growing business where you'll gain valuable exposure, broaden your accounting expertise, and continue progressing your finance career within a supportive and forward-thinking environment.

title: Probate Administrator
description:
Croydon Permanent Full-Time

Experienced Probate Administrator Required

Please note: This role is suitable only for candidates with previous hands-on probate administration experience. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider applicants whose experience is limited to general administration, legal administration in other areas of law, or academic study without practical probate casework experience.

We are seeking an experienced and highly organised Probate Administrator to join our growing and established estate planning and probate team in Croydon.

This is an excellent opportunity for an individual who has already worked within probate and estate administration and is looking to further their career within a specialist and expanding business. We are looking for someone who can confidently manage probate matters, support clients through the estate administration process, and make an immediate contribution to the team.

Due to continued growth and increasing workloads, we require someone with genuine probate experience who can quickly become a valuable member of a busy probate department.

The Role

As Probate Administrator, you will be responsible for assisting with the administration of estates from initial instruction through to completion. You will manage a varied caseload of probate matters, liaise with clients and third parties, prepare documentation, and ensure cases progress efficiently and accurately.

This role would suit somebody who has previously worked in a solicitor's probate department, probate specialist firm, estate administration company, trust corporation, or will-writing business dealing with probate matters.

Key Responsibilities
- Opening and managing probate files from instruction through to completion.
- Gathering estate information and corresponding with banks, investment providers, pension companies, and other financial institutions.
- Preparing probate applications and supporting documentation.
- Assisting with inheritance tax reporting and related estate administration tasks.
- Identifying and valuing estate assets and liabilities.
- Liaising with executors, beneficiaries, financial institutions, utility companies, and professional advisers.
- Maintaining accurate case notes and updating probate management systems.
- Monitoring file progression and proactively chasing outstanding information.
- Providing regular updates and excellent service to clients during what can be a sensitive and emotional time.
- Supporting the wider team to ensure matters are progressed efficiently and professionally.

Essential Experience

To be considered for this position, you must have:
- A minimum of 12 months' practical experience working within probate and estate administration.
- Experience preparing Probate Registry applications and related documentation.
- Experience dealing directly with executors, beneficiaries, banks, building societies, and other third-party organisations.
- A good working knowledge of the probate and estate administration process.
- Experience maintaining probate case files and managing multiple matters simultaneously.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Applications from candidates without practical probate administration experience are unlikely to be considered.

Desirable Experience
- Experience using Exizent or similar probate case management software.
- Knowledge of inheritance tax reporting and estate accounts.
- Experience dealing with trusts and charitable legacies.
- Previous employment within a solicitor's practice, probate specialist firm, trust corporation, or will-writing company.
- STEP qualification or studying towards a relevant qualification.

What We're Looking For

We are particularly interested in candidates who:
- Have genuine, hands-on probate administration experience.
- Can confidently manage probate files with minimal supervision.
- Take ownership of their workload and pay close attention to detail.
- Are compassionate and professional when supporting bereaved families.
- Want to build a long-term career within probate and estate administration.
- Thrive in a busy, client-focused environment.

What We Offer
- Competitive salary based on experience.
- Permanent, full-time position.
- Friendly and supportive working environment.
- Opportunity to further develop your probate expertise.
- Long-term career prospects within a growing specialist team.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
- Modern Croydon office location.

Location

This is an office-based role in Croydon and is not a remote or hybrid position.

- Contribute to SAUL's Quality Management System (QMS) and wider continuous improvement activities.

About You

We're looking for someone with strong administration and customer service skills who is comfortable working with data, systems and established processes.

Essential Experience & Skills
- GCSEs or equivalent experience, including Maths and English at GCSE Grade A C or equivalent.
- At least one year's administration experience.
- Experience working in an office environment.
- Experience using Microsoft products, particularly Outlook, SharePoint and Excel.
- Experience working with systems, processes and procedures.
- Strong accuracy and attention to detail, with the ability to follow instructions.
- Customer service experience.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good computer literacy.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
- Self-motivated with a positive attitude towards change.

Desirable

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller

£34,000 - £36,000 Central London Hybrid - 3 days office / 2 days home Permanent Immediate Start

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Credit Controller to join the finance team of a rapidly expanding international business based in Central London.

This is a varied credit control position within a commercially focused organisation where you'll have responsibility for a diverse customer ledger and work closely with colleagues across Finance, Sales and Operations.

The role would suit an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys having ownership of their accounts, building strong customer relationships and taking a proactive approach to recovering outstanding payments. NetSuite experience is highly desirable, as you'll be using the system regularly to monitor accounts, review balances and maintain accurate financial information.

About the Role:

As Credit Controller, you'll be responsible for keeping customer accounts up to date and ensuring outstanding invoices are followed up effectively.

You'll take a structured approach to your ledger, identifying overdue accounts, investigating issues and agreeing payment solutions with customers. You'll also work closely with internal departments where billing, contractual or account queries are preventing payment.

Experience dealing with complicated invoices, underpayments and legacy payments will be very beneficial. Further experience conducting investigations into aged debt and outstanding invoices will be very a great asset for this credit control role.

There may also be opportunities to support finance and operational teams during major events, giving the role a broader commercial dimension than a traditional credit control position.

Key Duties:
- Take day-to-day responsibility for an allocated customer ledger.
- Monitor outstanding invoices and carry out regular collection activity.
- Contact customers by telephone and email to agree payment dates and resolve overdue balances.
- Review aged debt and determine appropriate follow-up actions.
- Maintain accurate notes and records of collection activity.
- Investigate account discrepancies, invoice queries and disputed balances.
- Produce customer statements and respond to account-related enquiries.
- Work with Sales and other departments to resolve issues affecting payment.
- Reconcile customer and sales information between internal systems and NetSuite.
- Help minimise aged debt, credit notes and unallocated cash.
- Ensure payments are chased ahead of key event and operational deadlines.
- Maintain accurate customer account information.
- Deal confidently with customers across different markets and currencies.
- Provide assistance to on-site teams with customer payments when required.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have:
- Solid Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience.
- Previous experience using NetSuite.
- Good Excel skills.
- Experience dealing with multi-currency accounts and international customers.
- A good understanding of VAT and financial processes.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
- The confidence to deal with customers regarding overdue payments.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Good organisation and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A proactive approach to resolving problems rather than simply reporting them.
- Experience within events, exhibitions, media or another fast-moving commercial environment would be advantageous.

The Working Environment

The company has an informal and sociable culture, offering a refreshing alternative to a traditional corporate finance environment.

You'll be working in a relaxed office with a casual dress code, alongside a team that regularly gets together for social events, celebrations and nights out.

The business is continuing to grow internationally, so this is an opportunity to join a finance function where there is plenty of activity and exposure to different areas of the organisation.

Package:
- Salary: £34,000 - £36,000
- Location: Central London
- Hybrid: 3 days in the office / 2 days from home
- Start: Immediate
- Holiday: 25 days + 8 bank holidays
- Pension: Company pension scheme
- Additional benefits: Cycle to Work scheme and Season Ticket Loan

title: Credit Controller
description:
My client is looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join our Finance Department. The successful candidate will take responsibility for managing customer accounts, controlling credit exposure, collecting outstanding debts and ensuring customer accounts and payment allocations are accurate and up to date. The role requires close coordination with the Billing Department and regular reporting to the Finance Manager and Finance Director on collections and expected cash receipts for cash-flow planning.

Main Duties
- Proactively manage the sales ledger and collect outstanding customer debts by telephone and email.
- Monitor live customer balances, credit limits and credit utilisation daily.
- Contact customers approaching their credit limits and provide statements where required.
- Place customers exceeding their approved credit limit or payment terms on stop, and remove accounts from stop promptly once payment has been received and allocated.
- Communicate account stop/release information to the relevant operational departments.
- Contact customers before invoices become due to confirm invoices have been received, are correct and are approved for payment.
- Work closely with the Billing Department to resolve missing invoices, invoice queries and disputes promptly so that payments are not unnecessarily delayed.
- Maintain accurate expected payment dates and collection notes and provide the Finance Manager and Finance Director with regular updates on collections and expected cash receipts.
- Maintain and regularly review the aged debtor report, identifying overdue, disputed and high-risk accounts.
- Allocate customer receipts accurately to Sage, including BACS, cheque and credit-card payments.
- Reconcile daily credit-card transactions and receipts against payment-provider reports, the invoicing system and bank receipts.
- Maintain credit-card reconciliation records and investigate any differences promptly.
- Process and reconcile non-account/customer card transactions and related invoices, ensuring payments and invoices are correctly matched and recorded.
- Produce and issue customer statements and overdue-payment correspondence.
- Process credit-note requests, ensuring the correct supporting information and approval is obtained before credit notes are raised and issued.
- Record disputed invoices accurately and coordinate with Billing to ensure disputes are investigated and resolved.
- Evaluate new credit applications and carry out credit checks using Credit Reference Agencies.
- Maintain approved customer credit limits and payment terms.
- Complete regular reconciliations between Sage 50 Accounts Professional, Waste Logic and other relevant payment/invoicing systems.
- Deal promptly with customer account queries and manage the Credit Control mailbox.
- Ensure customer accounts, payment allocations, credit-control notes and supporting records remain accurate and fully up to date.

Experience & Skills

The successful candidate should have strong previous Credit Control experience and be confident managing a busy debtor ledger, chasing payments and dealing directly with customers. Experience of payment allocation, credit-card reconciliation, aged debt management, credit limits, account stops, customer reconciliations and invoice disputes is important.

The candidate must be proactive, organised and confident communicating with customers and internal departments. Strong attention to detail and reconciliation skills are essential. Experience using Sage 50 Accounts Professional is highly desirable, and experience with Waste Logic or similar waste-management/invoicing software would be an advantage. Previous experience within the construction, recycling, waste management or haulage industry would also be advantageous.

- Creating service charge accounts and ensuring financial transactions relating to completions are processed accurately and within required timescales.
- Coordinating property valuations and home demonstration appointments.
- Supporting operational compliance activities, audits, and business health checks.

What We're Looking For

We're seeking a proactive and detail-oriented individual who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and delivering excellent customer service.

Essential Experience & Skills
- Proven administration experience with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver to deadlines.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records and data.
- Excellent customer service and communication skills.
- Experience building productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong IT literacy, including experience using databases, CRM systems, and Microsoft Office applications.

Desirable
- Knowledge of Shared Ownership and Private Sale products.
- Understanding of property sales transactions and conveyancing processes.
- Interest in the housing or property sector.
- Experience working with Salesforce or similar CRM systems.

Metropolitan Thames Valley Housing (MTVH) provides affordable homes for people living across London, the South East, the East Midlands and the East of England.

Alongside housing, MTVH delivers a range of support services, working with residents who need additional help to live independently and well. This includes specialist support for older people, mental health services and transitional services that provide intensive support to people who are marginalised or vulnerable.

MTVH is committed to building strong, thriving communities. Through training programmes, events and activities, the organisation supports residents to improve employability, build skills and access opportunities that make a meaningful difference to their lives.

In line with the MTVH 2030 strategy ? Your Home, Your Service, Your Future ? diversity, equity and inclusion are central to how MTVH works. A range of colleague networks support gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation and disability, helping to create an inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging.

These networks provide a platform for colleagues to share their views, recognise what is working well and influence improvements. By listening, learning, and working together, MTVH continues to strengthen its culture, tackle business challenges and ensure it is serving people better every day.

title: Activity Co-ordinator
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Title: Activity Coordinator

Reports To: Service Manager or Team Leader

SOUTH WEST LONDON

Roles Reporting to this Position: None

Primary Objective: To design, coordinate and deliver a varied programme of engaging, accessible and employment-focused activities for young people aged 18 to 24. The role will build aspiration, confidence, resilience, transferable skills and understanding of workplace expectations, while working closely with Mentors and partners to help each participant progress towards suitable and sustainable employment, education or training.

Key Relationships/Interactions

Internal

Service Manager and Team Leader

Mentors and Employer Engagement and Employer Services colleagues

Quality, Compliance, Performance, Safeguarding and MI teams

Wider Delivery Colleagues

External

Participants (young people aged 18 to 24) and, where appropriate and with consent, their support networks

Engagement Activity Partners, specialist subcontractors and community organisations

Jobcentre Plus, local authorities, education and training providers

Local employers, sector partners and venue providers

Key Responsibilities

Activity Design and Delivery

Design, coordinate and maintain a rolling programme of structured group and individual activities aligned with participants needs, aspirations, action plans and outcomes.

Deliver welcoming, energetic and inclusive sessions for young people aged 18 to 24, using age-appropriate interests such as sport, creative arts, technology, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor activities and community projects.

Prepare clear session plans, learning objectives, resources and contingency arrangements so every activity supports employability, personal development or progression.

Adapt pace, content and delivery for different communication styles, neurodiversity, disabilities, literacy levels, digital capability, confidence levels and reasonable-adjustment needs.

Participant Engagement and Development

Use trauma-informed, strengths-based and culturally responsive practice to build trust, promote participant choice and voice, and support those who lack confidence or have had negative experiences of services or education.

Help participants develop communication, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, timekeeping, professional behaviours, digital skills and an understanding of workplace expectations.

Support young people to identify and present their transferable skills and achievements in CVs, applications, interviews and employer conversations.

Provide practical sector insight through employer talks, workplace visits, careers activities, mock recruitment exercises, volunteering and project-based learning.

Coordination and Partnership Working

Coordinate specialist partner delivery, including procurement or booking processes, schedules, venues, participant communications, accessibility, risk information, attendance, feedback and supporting evidence.

Work closely with Mentors to identify suitable activities, share relevant progress or concerns, and ensure learning is reflected in participant action plans and next steps.

Promote activities through engaging face-to-face and digital communications, use reminders and motivational contact, and promptly follow up non-attendance with the Mentor.

Build relationships with youth, community, education, health, specialist and employer partners to widen participation, strengthen referral routes and reduce barriers.

Contribute to programme events, outreach, sector pathways and employment-focused campaigns across sites and community venues.

Safeguarding, Inclusion and Professional Practice

Place participant welfare at the centre of delivery and follow safeguarding, lone-working, incident, whistleblowing and escalation procedures at all times.

Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns, disclosures, exploitation risks or changes in presentation. Apply adult safeguarding procedures for participants aged 18 to 24 and follow child safeguarding processes where a concern also involves a child.

Maintain professional boundaries, confidentiality and appropriate use of digital communication and social media.

Obtain and record informed consent where required, share information only where there is an appropriate and lawful basis and comply with data protection requirements.

Quality, Compliance and Performance

Complete activity and venue risk assessments, dynamic risk checks, incident reports and emergency arrangements in line with organisational policy and health and safety requirements.

Maintain accurate, timely and audit-ready records of referrals, attendance, participation, adjustments, feedback, progress, outcomes, risk documentation and safeguarding actions.

Deliver the agreed activity schedule consistently, ensuring sessions start on time and resources, venues and partners are coordinated effectively.

Monitor attendance, engagement and completion, take timely action to address non-engagement, and evidence improvements in confidence, employability skills, workplace understanding and readiness for next steps.

Use participant and stakeholder feedback, attendance data and progression information to evaluate impact and continuously improve the activity offer.

Support progression to agreed next steps, including mentoring actions, training, employer engagement, interviews, work experience or employment.

Manage activity resources and agreed budgets responsibly, demonstrate value for money, and ensure equipment is safe, available and stored appropriately.

Professional Knowledge and Flexibility

Maintain current knowledge of youth employment challenges, local labour markets, digital trends and support available to 18 to 24-year-olds.

Work flexibly across locations and, where required, outside standard hours to meet participant and programme needs.

To deliver role responsibilities in line with organisational values and all relevant policies and procedures

Any other duties appropriate to the level of this role, for which the post-holder has the necessary training or experience.

Essential and Desirable Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Delivery and Engagement

Experience of planning, coordinating and delivering engaging group activities for young people or young adults, preferably including those aged 18 to 24 and those not in education, employment or training or facing multiple barriers.

Strong facilitation, presentation and engagement skills, with the ability to build rapport while maintaining clear boundaries and expectations.

Ability to turn creative or recreational activities into purposeful employability and personal-development learning and adapt delivery for different needs, abilities, cultures, communication styles and confidence levels.

Experience in employability, youth work, community development, education, careers, coaching or publicly funded services, including delivery of creative, digital, sports, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor, volunteering or project-based activities.

Participant Support and Safe Practice

Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including low confidence, poor mental wellbeing, disability, neurodiversity, caring responsibilities, housing instability, transport difficulties, digital exclusion and limited work experience.

Knowledge of adult and child safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries, equality,

Qualifications, Values and Flexibility

A relevant qualification in youth work, teaching, training, coaching, careers, employability, safeguarding, mental health first aid or facilitation.

A current first-aid qualification and experience of completing activity or venue risk assessments.

Commitment to participant voice, strengths-based practice, inclusion and high-quality customer service.

Ability and willingness to travel on a daily basis to different locations within assigned local area, to support participants, employers, events, placements and contract delivery (no homeworking is available due to the nature of the role)

Willingness to complete all required induction and refresher training, including safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety.

Appointment is subject to checks appropriate to the role and participant group, which may include a DBS check where legally eligible and required.

You ll lead a varied programme of activities across our young person's accommodation services, bringing together opportunities around education, training and employment, life skills, wellbeing, creativity, sport, pre-tenancy preparation and personal development. Some sessions you ll deliver yourself; others you ll shape alongside colleagues, community organisations and specialist providers. The aim is simple: make the programme relevant, engaging and worth showing up for.

A big part of the role is understanding what can sit behind disengagement. You ll work creatively with young people who may be NEET (young people who are not currently in education, employment or training), have experienced trauma or struggled to engage with traditional services, using psychologically informed, trauma-informed and person-centred approaches to build trust and motivation. You ll also coach frontline colleagues to run effective activities of their own, helping opportunities become part of everyday life across the services.

This is a role with real scope to create, test and improve. You ll be part of a wider Opportunities team, sharing ideas and good practice while developing your own expertise in youth engagement, group work and programme delivery. You ll also have access to Single Homeless Project's (SHP) learning and development opportunities, helping you build specialist skills to grow your career across the organisation.

About you as our Youth Opportunities Coordinator:
- You know how to connect with young people who may be reluctant to engage, and can turn curiosity, creativity and persistence into meaningful participation.
- You have experience designing, coordinating or delivering engaging groups, activities or programmes for young people.
- You understand trauma-informed and psychologically informed ways of working, and can balance empathy, professional boundaries and appropriate challenge.
- You re confident building relationships with colleagues, community organisations and specialist services to open up new opportunities for young people.
- You re organised, adaptable and full of ideas, with the confidence to take ownership of a programme while working collaboratively with others

- Problem solver.
- Ability to work under pressure, whilst maintaining attention to detail.

Property Management Administrator
- This role is a pivotal position. The main focus is the issues surrounding property maintenance, property management and deposit resolution at the end of the tenancy. It requires a special talent to keep both the landlord and tenant 'on side'. For example, sometimes a tenant can get quite stressed when there is a relatively minor delay on the repair of a washing machine etc.

Pertemps Recruitment Partnership is seeking an experienced Legal Assistant to join HB Public Law, the shared legal service supporting a number of North West London boroughs and Home Counties local authorities.
This is an excellent opportunity for a legal professional to work within a specialist public-sector legal environment, supporting a team of lawyers and having conduct of legal matters across areas including property, planning, regeneration, contracts and procurement.
The successful candidate will work as part of a specialist legal team, providing high-quality legal advice and support to public-sector clients while developing their legal knowledge, case management and client-facing skills.
Key Responsibilities
- Provide legal advice and support on commercial matters including property, planning, regeneration, contracts and procurement.
- Provide legal research and support to lawyers and colleagues across the service.
- Manage a significant caseload in accordance with Lexcel requirements and maintain high standards of client care.
- Draft legal documents, correspondence, pleadings and other relevant documentation.
- Contribute to keeping clients and colleagues informed of relevant developments in law and policy.
- Use electronic case management systems and Microsoft Office products effectively.
- Undertake legal research and ensure accurate recording of instructions, advice and case information.
- Represent clients, where appropriate, at courts, tribunals, panels and external meetings.

Requirements
The successful candidate will ideally have:
- A qualification in law, such as a Law Degree, CPE or LPC, or be studying towards/hold another recognised legal qualification.
- Alternatively, substantial experience working within a legal environment may be considered in lieu of formal qualifications.
- Knowledge of English law, practice and procedure relating to property, planning, regeneration, contracts and/or procurement.
- Knowledge and understanding of public law principles within a local government environment.
- Experience managing a legal caseload with appropriate levels of supervision.
- Strong legal research, drafting and case management skills.
- Evidence of continuing professional development.

For candidates applying, experience of handling more complex matters with minimal supervision will be required. Candidates will also need to hold CILEX Fellow status and be entitled to use the Chartered Legal Executive Lawyer title, or hold an equivalent qualification.

For almost 60 years, Pertemps Recruitment Partnership has been a market leader in providing temporary and permanent staffing solutions. title: Administration Assistant
description:
Job Summary

We are looking for a bright and articulate team player with excellent IT and interpersonal skills to join our vibrant team. Your role will give you a broad exposure to the workings of a Ofsted rated Outstanding Fostering Agency and Children's Homes.

You will need a keen attention to detail, brilliant communication and excellent use of systems including Microsoft Excel.

Main Duties and Responsibilities
- To provide comprehensive administrative support to the Team Coordinator, Senior Management, the Social Work and Residential Teams and Fostering Panel
- Co-ordinating the collation of HR information required for the recruitment of new staff for Ascent Children Services, including social workers/administrators/residential team/ Form F assessors and Panel Members, staff across the residential and fostering agency. This involves co-ordinating requests for reference checks, DBS etc., medicals and liaising with the Team Coordinator, Social Work team and senior management in relation to the status of these checks
- Supporting the approval and regular receipt of information required for the registration of Foster Carers. This includes carrying out checks and references for new foster carers and back up foster carers and monitoring returns and recording receipts on Social Care IT systems of both prospective foster carers, foster carers.
- To coordinate, plan and disseminate appropriate forms for Foster Carers' annual reviews. Ensure dates for reviews are agreed upon within the approval timescales in conjunction with SSWs, IRO, foster carers, LASW and young people.Ensure reports are completed, signed and where necessary ready for presentation to the Panel
- Disseminate Foster Carer Agreements to carers, ensure correct approval terms are noted and upload returned signed agreement to charms.
- Assist Team coordinator with the preparation of Fostering Panel meetings, ensure case correspondence is uploaded by deadlines, and circulate notifications to Panel members and SSWs involved with specific Panel meetings. Attend Panel meetings to minute take, liaise with the Panel Chair to agree on final minutes and upload final minutes to Dropbox and Charms.
- Take minutes of meetings including fostering Panels, team meetings, HR meetings and foster carer support meetings, providing accurate typed records and disseminating records within agreed timescales
- Data inputting on electronic systems, including the CHARMS, Citation and ClearCare, competent in Microsoft Office (Word/Excel)
- Training and Social Events - Administer carers and team annual training and social calendar, sending out texts and email notifications and reminders to carers and staff. Coordinating room bookings, sending out advanced training text/email reminder alerts to carers, liaising, with course facilitators and assisting with course correspondence in advance of course, preparing and distribution of carers course notes handouts, process and distribution of carers course certificates, coordinate Ascent Carers team meetings, update carers individual training profiles and course attendance log, arrange catering and refreshments for training sessions, present refreshments and lunches and tidy away after sessions, undertake any other duties required by the Team Coordinator, Senior ManagementTeam and SSW's
- Support the running of the Office. This includes responding to all telephone/email or in person visitor enquiries respectfully and communicate effectively and appropriately
- Where necessary support the team with marketing; responding to calls and enquiries, taking applicant details, sending out letters and information packs and assisting the team at outside events
- Facilities management - supporting the team coordinator with any facilities operations/purchases
- To respect confidentiality and to comply with your duty of confidentiality to all stakeholders in the Agency. Ensure all information is stored safely and securely

Person Specification

Knowledge and Experience
- Experience of working in an administrative role or customer service environment where multi-tasking and decision-making skills are successfully demonstrated
- Experience of working with IT systems, data entry and use of Microsoft Office.
- Demonstrates excellent customer service skills
- Possesses confident and persuasive professional telephone skills
- Proven track record in managing a demanding and varied workload
- Demonstrates understanding of effective teamwork
- Knowledge and understanding of Social Services, in particular, the provision of services for children

Qualifications
- Achievement of a minimum of two A levels, or equivalent
- Good range of GCSE passes to include English and Math's

Aptitudes and Abilities
- Good interpersonal skills; effective at quickly establishing and building good working relationships internally and externally, at all levels
- Self-sufficient and self-motivated with the ability to work independently, recognizing when matters need input from or referral to others
- Analytical, with high attention to detail and a logical approach to problem-solving
- Confident user on IT systems including Microsoft Excel.
- Multitasker who can manage, prioritise and monitor own work
- Contributes positively to teams, encouraging and facilitating the contribution of others and working sensitively with team colleagues
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively negotiate and influence, especially on the phone
- Decisive with a determination to rise to the challenge, offering creative solutions to overcome difficulties

Disposition
- Anticipates and responds proactively to problems, knowing when to seek guidance
- Able to work on own initiative, recognizing when reference needs to be made to others
- Able to work and make effective decisions under pressure
- A calm and assured approach to work
- Well-organized and a clear thinker
- Able to work individually and as part of a team
- Resilient
- Willing to work flexibly and to strict deadlines
- Able to work on occasion outside of normal office hours

title: Contracts Coordinator
description:
We are currently recruiting a permanent Contracts Coordinator to join our busy Contracts Office based at our Romford office.

This is a varied, fast-paced role combining client and temporary worker coordination, payroll administration, compliance, and customer service. We are looking for someone who is highly organised and accurate, but equally important is having the confidence and personality to communicate with clients and temporary workers throughout the day. You will be working as part of an established team, helping to manage and coordinate our temporary workforce and ensuring our Blue Chip clients receive an excellent level of service. You will help ensure shifts are fully covered, client requirements are met and any issues are dealt with quickly and professionally.

What We Are Looking For:

We are looking for someone who is outgoing, confident, and naturally comfortable talking to people. You should be happy picking up the telephone, building relationships with clients and workers. You will be working in a busy environment where priorities can change quickly, so you must be able to multi-task, work at speed and remain accurate under pressure. There is also a significant amount of compliance, payroll information and paperwork involved, making excellent attention to detail essential. Previous experience of payroll input or timesheet processing is required, while a background in sales administration, recruitment, customer service or another client-facing administrative role would be advantageous.

Strong Excel and Microsoft Office skills are important, as is the ability to juggle several priorities at once, We need someone with energy, initiative and a strong work ethic who is not afraid to get involved, support the wider team and learn new things. If you have previously worked in sales administration or recruitment, even better - you already understand the importance of great customer service, strong relationships and making things happen.

Key Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing and coordinating temporary workers to ensure client shifts are covered and run smoothly
- Preparing, checking, and inputting weekly timesheets onto the Merit payroll system and others
- Chasing outstanding timesheets, hours and other information required to meet strict payroll deadlines
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with existing clients
- Providing comprehensive administrative support to the existing team
- Conducting pre-screening of potential applicants
- Following the relevant compliance procedures and strict applicant registration processes
- Providing a high level of customer service to clients and temporary workers, both over the telephone and face to face

Experience within sales administration or recruitment would be particularly advantageous.

Benefits include:
- A day off for your birthday every year
- Christmas Party/annual company events
- Performance related bonus/incentive scheme
- Generous holiday entitlement increasing with length of service
- Long-service recognition reward schemes
- Opportunities to take part in our Christmas Savings Scheme

Hours of work: Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 5.00pm

Interested?

If you are a confident people-person who is also a strong and accurate administrator, enjoy working in a busy environment and aren't afraid to pick up the phone and get things done, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to join our Contracts Office in Romford.

Vulnerable Adults, Children & Young People All members of staff have a duty to safeguard and promote the welfare of vulnerable adults, children and young people in all relevant areas of their work. This will include timely attendance at relevant training events and compliance with practice procedures. Personal/Professional Development You will participate in any training or development programme implemented by the practice as part of your employment. This will include: Participating in an annual development review including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of your own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for your own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Keeping abreast of legislative changes and guidance relating to your role. Quality You will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess your own performance and take accountability for your own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on your own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage your own time, workload and resources. Communication You should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.
